note: Historical review of every snapshot in Müller-Crepon col_units_full.geojson (doi:10.7910/DVN/9JI06R), read by scripts/histsurveys/mullercrepon.mjs. Per snapshot: which field holds the first-level subdivision of the polity CShapes draws there that year (region | district | exclude), the in-force interval where dated reorganisations establish it (to exclusive; otherwise the snapshot year only), units to drop, clear typo corrections, sovereign where the data has neither colbrit nor colfrnc, and sources. A snapshot missing here fails the harvest.

AGO 1920.why: The six-district set (Loanda, Congo, Mossamedes, Huilla, Benguella, Lunda) is the c.1900–1910 layout (EB1911 still counts five districts with Huilla as the hinterland of Mossamedes); no source places this set in force in 1920, by when further districts (e.g. Malanje, Bié, Moxico, Cuanza) are attested in later layouts. Frame also lies 8.2% outside CShapes Angola. Cannot date the layout.

sources.title: Encyclopædia Britannica 1911, "Angola"
sources.says: Angola is divided into five districts (Congo, Loanda, Benguella, Mossamedes, Lunda); Huilla described as the hinterland portion of Mossamedes.

BWA 1899.why: Units are native reserves defined by Proclamation 9 of 1899 (named after chiefs: Sekgoma, Bathoen, Linchwe, Sebele, Khama), Crown land ("Protectorate") and the Tati Concession — land-tenure categories, not administrative divisions. The first-level divisions in 1899 were the Northern and Southern Protectorate (Assistant Commissioners), which are not present.

BWA 1906.why: The Protectorate was administered in two divisions, Northern Protectorate (AC at Palapye, from 1903/4 Francistown) and Southern Protectorate (AC at Gaberones), from 1891 until the AC posts lapsed in 1923. The region field holds exactly these two. Range applies to the two-division set; the internal N/S line itself is only known from this map.

CAF 1938.why: Frame (735,280 km²) extends ~114,000 km² into Chad and includes Chadian units (Gounou[-Gaya], Maro). Southern Chad (Moyen-Chari, Logone, Mayo-Kebbi) was attached to Oubangui-Chari 1925–32 and Nov 1934–Apr 1936, and returned to Chad on 1936-04-29; so the map shows a pre-1936 layout, not 1938. The companion TCD 1938 lacks exactly this southern area.

CAF 1946.why: The 11 distinct units correspond one-to-one with the chef-lieux of the Oubangui-Chari régions of the late 1940s (Bangui, Mbaïki=Lobaye, Berbérati=Haute-Sangha, Bossangoa=Ouham, Bozoum=Ouham-Pendé, Fort-Sibut=Kémo-Gribingui, Bambari=Ouaka, Mobaye=Basse-Kotto, Bangassou=Mbomou, Ndélé=Dar-el-Kouti, Birao=Vakaga); the publisher labels them by seat, not by the région name — IntMap should not present a seat label as the unit's official name. Frame matches CShapes (1.6% outside). No dated decree found bounding the set.

CIV 1937.polity: Côte d'Ivoire incl. former Upper Volta cercles 1932–1947 (CShapes)
CIV 1937.why: After Upper Volta's dissolution (1932-09-05) Côte d'Ivoire held the southern Voltaic cercles directly; all 26 units were cercles under the lieutenant-governor. The decree of 1937-07-13 (JORF 1937-07-21) created the région administrative de la Haute-Côte-d'Ivoire grouping Ouagadougou, Kaya, Tenkodogo, Koudougou, Gaoua and Bobo-Dioulasso, after which those cercles were no longer first level — so this layout ends at that decree (frame matches CShapes 1 July 1937 to 15 km²). Start of the exact set not established.

COD 1910.why: The 12 units are exactly the 1910 set (Bas-Congo formed from Banana, Boma, Matadi, Cataractes; Katanga a vice-government general). Superseded by the arrêté royal of 1912-03-28 (22 districts). The l'Uele unit still includes the Lado Enclave, transferred to Sudan in June 1910 (~2.3% of the frame lies outside CShapes).

COD 1933.why: EXCLUDED: IntMap already draws these six provinces from its own dossier scripts/histrecon/dossiers/COD.json, from the reorganisation that created them (1933-10-01, dated with sources) to independence. This sheet states the same units for the year 1933 only — from 1 January, nine months before they existed — and, being a publisher's record, would displace the dated rows (the dossier yields to publishers).
